$comment: Operational workflow authoring contract (Wave 3, a1). A workflow definition DECLARES the shape a run takes: the base ref it targets, the concurrency it obeys, the workspace it runs in, the steps that produce + verify candidates, and the promotion contract that advances a candidate once its required gates pass. Operational STATUS is never authored here — a run's status (running/succeeded/awaiting approval/…) is derived from run evidence, never declared (completion follows the revision). The JSON Schema below expresses the structural contract; the semantic rules a schema alone cannot express (a mutating step needs downstream verification, a gate must be bound to a candidate, a required gate's evidence must be machine-executed, promotion needs required gates, prompt text is not evidence) are enforced by workflows/lint_workflow.py.
title: Operational Workflow (workflow-v1)
description: The authoring contract for a new operational workflow. Validate with JSON Schema draft 2020-12 and run workflows/lint_workflow.py for the semantic rules.

apiVersion.description: The versioned schema family this definition validates against.

kind.description: The document kind. Only 'Workflow' is valid for this schema.

revision.description: The definition's version identifier. A run certifies only its exact revision — an edited definition is a new revision, not a re-run of the old one.

lifecycle.description: The authored lifecycle claim of the DEFINITION. This is not an operational run status — how far a run has progressed is derived from run evidence, never written here.

description.description: Optional human description of what the workflow does.

metadata.description: Identity + lifecycle of the workflow definition. There is deliberately NO operational status field (status: running/completed/… is derived from run evidence, never authored).

baseRef.description: The git ref (branch or sha) the workflow is rooted from and that a promotion advances candidates toward (promote.py's --base, conventionally 'main').

mode.description: isolated: each run executes in its own throwaway worktree/clone off baseRef. shared: steps execute against a shared checkout. readonly: the run may only read (a measurement/research shape that produces no candidate to promote).

image.description: Default container image for the workflow's steps when a step does not name its own.

group.description: The concurrency group this workflow belongs to. Runs of workflows sharing a group are governed by the same policy.

policy.description: serial: at most one run of the group executes at a time. bounded: at most maxRuns concurrent runs (maxRuns required). parallel: no workflow-level cap (fleet-level leases still apply).

maxRuns.description: Concurrency ceiling; REQUIRED when policy is 'bounded'.

steps.description: The ordered plan of steps. Edges: 'needs' names the steps this step depends on; 'candidateFrom' names the step whose produced candidate this step consumes.

id.description: Unique step id within the workflow (referenced by needs/candidateFrom/requiredGates).

kind.description: agent: an LLM-authored work step (produces a candidate). task: a deterministic command/image step (build, sync, measure — produces a candidate when it writes). gate: a verification checkpoint bound to a candidate, run by a machine executor. approval: a controller/human checkpoint bound to a candidate.

executor.description: The mechanism that runs the step. agent: an LLM agent phase. test: the independent test-suite verifier (the sole source of truth for test_executed_success). command: a deterministic command/image execution. human: a controller/operator decision. Defaults per kind: agent->agent, task->command, approval->human; a gate must name a machine executor (test|command) when it is required.

image.description: Container image for the step (overrides the workspace default).

scope.description: The step's capability scope (the machine's five-scope vocabulary). Default: implementation in a write workspace, research_readonly in a readonly workspace. Write-capable scopes (implementation/review_readonly/proposal_write) mark agent/task steps as MUTATING.

needs.description: Step ids this step depends on (the workflow DAG edges).

candidateFrom.description: The id of the mutating step whose candidate sha this step consumes/gates. A gate or approval step resolves its candidate here, or from its single mutating upstream.

gate.description: An inline self-gate on a mutating step, bound to that step's OWN produced candidate. The executor is a machine check (test|command), so an inline gate can never be prose-only.

prompt.description: Instruction text for an agent/task step. Prompt text is scaffolded instructions — it is NEVER evidence for a required gate (a required gate's evidence comes from its executor).

description.description: Optional human description of the step.

blocking.description: Whether a failed gate blocks the step from completing (and its candidate from advancing). Default true.

executor.description: The machine check that produces the gate evidence. test: the test-suite verifier. command: a deterministic command.

candidateFrom.description: The id of the mutating step whose final candidate this workflow promotes.

strategy.description: How the candidate integrates into baseRef once its required gates pass. squash-merge is promote.py's implemented strategy; merge-commit/fast-forward declare intent for future executors.

requiredGates.description: The gate/approval step ids that must pass before promotion. Each entry must reference a real gate or approval step (never a mutating step, never prompt text).
